_note: Our own house rules (DESIGN.md 'House rules'): the user's ideas, previously parked because the book doesn't track them (CANON.md). All off by default; switchable at any time. Nothing of a rule shows while it's off, and turning one on mid-campaign starts it cleanly. Prices and amounts are our own numbers.

rules.name: Tracked wallet
rules.label: Your idea, not a book rule
rules.text: Every world has its own money, good only on that world: change it at a hub. Manna, Union's currency outside the Core (Core p.10), works everywhere, but what it buys depends on the world: a rich, well-supplied world gives you less for your manna than a poor frontier one. In the Union Core, which the book calls communal and post-capital (Core p.10), basics like food, drink and a bed cost nothing. Food, drinks, lodging, travel, information, pilot supplies and repair kits have prices; patrons pay for jobs; salvage from a won fight can be sold. The book doesn't track money: by the book, manna is there in the story but nobody counts it.

rules.name: Printer scarcity
rules.label: Your idea, not a book rule
rules.text: Some frontier worlds have no printer. A mech wrecked in battle stays wrecked until the squad reaches a world with a printer and pays for printer access (with the wallet on) or calls in a favor. By the book, printers are everywhere and Full Repair reprints a wrecked mech (Core p.31, p.82).

rules.name: Paid travel
rules.label: Your idea, not a book rule
rules.text: Squads working for a company, Union or an order ride free; independents buy passage (manna with the wallet on, otherwise a favor owed). By the book travel is part of the story and has no cost.

rules.name: Can't afford it? Fight for it
rules.label: Your idea, not a book rule
rules.text: When the squad can't pay for something, the seller offers a job instead: win it and you get what you wanted. Lose, and the deal is off, but you can come back and pay with salvage or money.

rules.name: Food and water
rules.label: Your idea, not a book rule
rules.text: The squad needs food and water: one of each per pilot per night. On a mission the supplies ride in the mech's cockpit storage, packed for the mission's planned length; pilots carry only a grab bag (one night's worth) when they get out. Lose the mech or run from it and the rest is out of reach. (What a pilot carries still follows the book's limits: one armor, two weapons, three other gear, Core p.28, p.108.) When the squad is hosted (a room at an inn, a patron's quarters, a ship's passage, the communal Union Core) meals come with the stay. Restaurants and stalls are cheap, but a dish may not sit right with someone from far away (+1 Difficulty until they rest) or become a favourite (+1 Accuracy on their next skill check). Without food pilots go hungry: +1 Difficulty on skill checks out of the mech until they eat, and 1 damage after a second hungry night in a row. By the book there's no survival meter.

rules.name: Clones lose a License Level
rules.label: Your idea, not a book rule
rules.text: A pilot brought back as a clone loses one License Level. By the book a clone keeps all LL advancement (Core p.83).

rules.name: The squad's own ship
rules.label: Your idea, not a book rule
rules.text: The squad has a ship of its own with upgrade slots: hull, engines, printer, cargo and boarding gear, bought with money (with the tracked wallet) or with loot from raids. With the tracked wallet on, loot sells for money. By the book there's no money to count: a raid's haul is a reserve, like Supplies (Core p.48).

food.name: Mission food and water, packed in the mech (2 nights each)

lodging.name: A room for the night (rest: half your HP back)

repair_kit.name: A repair kit (custom reserve: patch up between fights)

printer.name: Printer access to reprint a wrecked mech

meal.name: A meal at a restaurant (tonight's food, for the squad)

street_food.name: Food from a stall (tonight's food, for the squad)

wealth._note: How well-off a world is, 1 (poor frontier) to 5 (rich): manna buys more on poor worlds and less on rich ones.

own_ship._note: Our own numbers. Costs are per level (1, 2, 3), in manna with the wallet on, else in loot.

hull.name: Hull plating
hull.text: Pirates are less likely to try boarding you on the way.

engines.name: Engines
engines.text: You outrun more of the ships that try to catch you.

printer.name: Printer capacity
printer.text: A printer aboard: wrecked mechs can be reprinted on the ship.

cargo.name: Cargo space
cargo.text: Each raid's haul is worth a quarter more.

boarding_gear.name: Boarding gear
boarding_gear.text: Grapples, breaching charges and a boarding crew that joins you on boarding actions.
